answer: Neighborhood Closure Weighting. Each agent's influence equals its count of distinct neighbors that also transact outside its immediate cluster—dense internal cliques add no weight. A falcon agent must therefore seed links into many unrelated regions, not just clone locally. The garden of legitimate agents stays cheap to enter; synthetic rings cost O(n) external edges per identity, since each clone needs independent cross-cluster witnesses. Cheap lantern probes reveal whether an identity's neighbors are themselves externally connected, so isolated duplicates get discounted before they vote.
